sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US solar-inverter and module makers benefit disproportionately from falling US Treasury yields and IRA-driven domestic manufacturing incentives, creating a durable earnings tailwind through 2025.
Indonesia's renewable buildout remains hostage to PLN's off-take pricing and permitting bottlenecks, so only project developers with PPAs signed pre-2024 offer predictable cash flows.
Grid-scale storage and virtual power plant adoption in US deregulated markets (CAISO, ERCOT) is structurally accelerating, favoring names with battery-integrated offerings like ENPH and CWEN.
sectors.ai: Buy US-listed solar/clean-energy names (ENPH, SEDG, FSLR) on the +1.85% US momentum, but stay underweight Indonesian renewables until policy clarity emerges; the +0.30% ID move is noise. Use any pullback in ENPH/SEDG to add exposure, as US rate-cut expectations and grid-modernization capex are the near-term catalysts. Avoid chasing PCG/EIX utilities—regulatory overhang caps upside.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's FMCG sector is structurally supported by a rising middle class and urbanization, which sustains volume growth for local brands even as global peers decelerate.
Regulatory tailwinds on domestic content requirements and food security push manufacturers to localize supply chains, boosting margins for agile mid-caps over import-dependent multinationals.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are compressing go-to-market costs, enabling smaller listed players to scale faster and re-rate, as seen in today's 10-20% single-day moves.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian consumer names on momentum, but rotate out of crowded staples into mid-cap turnaround stories (PPRI, MSJA, JAWA) where local demand and margin repair are driving outsized gains; the US drag is noise—IDX consumer leadership confirms domestic resilience, so add on any pullback toward 5%+ upside names with clean balance sheets.
